findings.title: Missing API Key in Development Environment
findings.description: The dashboard .env file has API_KEY commented out, running without authentication in development mode
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to dashboard API in development environment
findings.recommendation: Set API_KEY even in development to match production security posture
findings.remediation: Generate API key with: openssl rand -hex 32 and set in .env
findings.notes: Development mode - acceptable for local testing

findings.title: Environment Files Present in Repository
findings.description: Found .env files in dashboard/ and llm-mesh/ directories
findings.impact: Potential exposure of sensitive configuration if not properly gitignored
findings.recommendation: Verify .env files are in .gitignore and never committed
findings.remediation: Already in .gitignore - verify with: git check-ignore -v dashboard/.env

findings.title: Executable Scripts Found
findings.description: Found 236 executable shell and JavaScript files in repository
findings.impact: Ensure only authorized scripts are executable
findings.recommendation: Review executable permissions regularly, remove unnecessary execute bits
findings.notes: Scripts in scripts/ directory are expected to be executable

findings.title: Rate Limiting Configuration Review
findings.description: Dashboard configured with rate limiting: 100 requests per 15 minutes, 10 for control endpoints
findings.impact: Adequate for development, may need adjustment for production load
findings.recommendation: Monitor rate limit hit rates and adjust for production usage

findings.title: CORS Allowed Origins
findings.recommendation: Update for production deployment with specific allowed origins
findings.remediation: N/A - current configuration appropriate for development

findings.title: Comprehensive .gitignore Coverage
findings.description: Repository has well-configured .gitignore for sensitive files
findings.impact: Good protection against accidental secret commits

secrets_scanning.details: No hardcoded secrets found in tracked files. Only configuration references to tokens/keys found in JSON metadata (tokens_used, token_budget, etc.)

sensitive_files.details: .env files found but properly gitignored. No .key, .pem, or credentials files found in repository

access_controls.details: API authentication configured, rate limiting in place, CORS properly restricted

file_permissions.details: Scripts have appropriate execute permissions. No world-writable files detected

recommendations.rationale: Match production security posture even in development

recommendations.recommendation: Implement pre-commit hooks for secret scanning
Document security configuration in dedicated security policy

system_health.note: Some services offline but not blocking security audit

conclusion: The commit-relay repository demonstrates good security practices with proper .gitignore configuration, rate limiting, CORS restrictions, and no hardcoded secrets. The main areas for improvement are enabling API authentication in development and implementing automated secret scanning. Overall security posture is ACCEPTABLE for development environment.
